title: bls12-381-fixed-g1-invert-g2: Frobenius-class-folded distinguished-point rho in GT

claims.statement: For uniform nonidentity P in G1 and independent uniform z in GT (identity included), the sequential classical algorithm of proof.md returns Q in G2 with e(P,Q)=z with probability at least 0.39 over (P,z) and the algorithm's coins, using at most 2^125.84 total target-group-operation equivalents (dense Fp12 multiplication = 1, C = 20,000), including every table construction, pairing, start, step, probe, report, store operation, replay, verification and output step. The algorithm sets g = e(P,Q0), solves z = g^a by a distinguished-point rho walk on the 12-element Frobenius classes of GT (x ~ x^p, which acts as x -> x^lambda with lambda = p mod r of order 12) and outputs Q = [a]Q0. The class walk uses a 3-multiplication Frobenius-covariant selector (its seed d = Re(gamma*conj(c1)) is g0*(a-b), one multiplication, because the tower constant gamma is exactly g0*(1-u) with g1 = -g0, an exact congruence the package's algebra check asserts on production data), whose twelve class keys are minimised on the six stored values and their negations through one negation of their maximum rather than six materialised negations (the same key and twist, checked exhaustively on 117,649 six-tuples and against the direct twelve-value scan on real GT elements and their conjugates), an R = 2^14 table of twisted multipliers, a 24-class look-back window held as a 24-slot ring of keys with a sorted one-byte index array and an inverse map (so an accept is a ring write plus one rotation of at most 23 index bytes, and membership is the same five-step binary search over the same 24 keys), deterministic probing, distinguished-point density 2^-80, trail cap 2^87, and exponent recovery by replaying the two colliding trails. Each multiplication slot is charged 1 + 2053/20000 units: 2,053 instructions itemised in proof.md section 5 as 2,041 of hard per-item bounds plus a 0.588% margin, the table index being the low 14 bits of the first of the two 64-bit hash words of the class key and the 80 distinguished-point bits being that word's 64 bits plus 16 from the second. The accepted-step budget is S_max = ceil(sqrt(2*mu*N*U)), with N = (r-1)/12 classes, mu = 11/10, x = 3903/10000, L = -ln(1-x) = ln(10000/6097), and U = sum_{k=1}^{64} x^k/k + x^65/(65(1-x)), an exact rational upper bound for L with 0 < U - L < 2^-99 (the computed gap is 6.63e-31). The ledger uses U, the larger rational bound: S_max is the least integer with S_max^2 >= 2*mu*N*U, checked in integers, the L-based ceiling being a different integer about 2^25.46 steps lower, and the total work computed from U is at most a relative 2^-99 above the total that exact L would give. The target main-event probability is 0.3903, giving total work at most 2^125.83841; the claim 2^125.84 is the least hundredth at or above log2 W, proved directly by the exact integer inequalities W^100 <= 2^12584 and W^100 > 2^12583 on the exact rational total W formed from this S_max, so no smaller hundredth suffices. Preprocessing is at most 2^24.13 units and is included in the total; nonuniform advice is none (0 bytes); peak memory is at most 2^54 bytes (at most 2^47 store records of 96 bytes, a 113 MB twist table and under 2^20 bytes of state), all within one 2^64-byte address space. Success is a heuristic claim and rests on disclosed hypotheses: H1 (random-mapping birthday behaviour of the class walk with walk-quality loss at most mu = 11/10 and negligible coalescence loss), H2 (pseudorandomness of the two hash words of the class key, which give the uniform table index and the distinguished-point predicate, and iid uniform twist offsets for distinct classes), H3 (ideal algorithm coins). Under H1-H3 the main-event probability is at least 3903/10000 at S_max and all other losses (stated in proof.md section 6) are below 2.7e-4, so the success probability is at least 0.39003 > 0.39. This is a classical cold attack with no uncharged advice and no quantum steps; it is an analytic claim, not a production-scale execution.

experiments.purpose: One bounded run of four parts, none of which is a production-scale run. (1) ledger: recompute the exact work ledger of proof.md section 5 (S_max, M_max, the itemised per-slot instructions, the additive items, log2 W_max <= claim with the exact integer checks W^100 <= 2^12584 and W^100 > 2^12583, and that the selector's priced two-half minimum equals the direct twelve-value scan on 117,649 six-tuples), the memory ledger and the trap-lemma bound of section 7 (arithmetic on the stated prices only, no instruction counts measured). (2) algebra: on real BLS12-381 GT elements check lambda = p mod r has order 12 with lambda^6 = -1, Frobenius equals x -> x^lambda, the tower constants satisfy gamma = g0*(1-u) (g1 = -g0), g0^6 = -1/8 and zeta = 2*g0^2, the 3-multiplication selector gives the same 12 values as the general g0*a + g1*b form and those values equal the true first coordinates of c1(sigma^k(y)), the two-half minimum returns the same key and twist as the direct twelve-value scan on the element and on all twelve conjugates, the class key is Frobenius invariant, k* is covariant, and the twisted walk step is class-equivariant. (3) toy: run the complete algorithm (selector, twisted table, look-back window with probing, distinguished points, store, replay with exponent tracking, Frobenius alignment, g^a == z) over a toy tower of the production shape with real Fp12 arithmetic and a 22-23 bit subgroup, checking recovered logarithms and that tracked replays reproduce the untracked paths. (4) sim: exponent-domain emulation of the identical walk with the production table size, measuring the walk-quality constant mu_hat at the first inter-trail class repeat against an ideal value 1 and a plain-birthday control, the fraction of groups whose first repeat falls inside the S_max budget (the statistic the claim uses; ideal map 0.4197, required 0.3903), the escape rate against 1/(12R), and whether meeting trails reach the same distinguished point. Toy sizes only; extrapolation to production is a disclosed heuristic (proof.md sections 6 and 9).
